summary: A small cast-iron tower on an island at the mouth of Cutler Harbor, Maine, relit in 2001 after 26 dark years and now owned by the American Lighthouse Foundation.

notes_for_editor: Disagreements stated in the text: first-lit year (1847 archive vs spring 1848 LighthouseFriends vs 1846 per some sources); tower height (35 ft to lantern centre per NRHP vs 41 ft per archive/LF); Corbett's dates (1923-44 archive vs 1921-39 D'Entremont); Colbeth (archive roster 1944-46 vs LF dismissal July 1950); dark period (LF 26 years; D'Entremont says 21). Station record says first_lit 1847 and 1976 second tower; not changed. Light-House Board reports before 1891 are not in the corpus, so 1847-1890 material rests on LighthouseFriends (copyrighted; paraphrased). The inspector's 1850 remarks and Lewis 1842 words are quoted second-hand via LighthouseFriends. Roster dates for 1950s-70s keepers are archive spans, not appointments; several Coast Guard names are in the archive's USCG list. Fog-signal outcome after 1903 not verified (no Board reports 1902-1914 in corpus); LF says never built. 1894 fog-bell survey page cited by scan page 721 (printed number uncertain); 1893 Board report p.42 header confirmed on OCR. No 'record corrections' proposed; the record's 'Sources differ on whether the light is still lit' is answered by the archive: active (VLB-44 solar, 2019). NRHP listing date 14 March 1988 is from TravelMaine (secondary).
